data.narrative:
Cradle, a Series B biotech and health company, has raised $102.7M to date across its founding team of five. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of three same-sector, same/adjacent-stage private companies (Colossal Biosciences at $10.3B Series C, Chai Discovery at $3.8B Series C, and New Limit at $3.1B Series C), supplemented by three public biotech comparables (RXRX, TEM, ONT.L).

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for post-money value, applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical of Series B advancement, yielding $195M. Peer-median analysis across the three private comparables produces $3.8B, though this range spans $3.1B to $10.3B—reflecting significant dispersion in the cohort. Public-comp anchoring (median P/S of 7.4x) cannot be applied due to absence of revenue disclosure, standard for private companies.

The triangulated valuation range spans $166M (low) to $4.4B (high), with a median of $2.0B derived from two methods. The stage-progression method anchors the floor; peer-median anchors the ceiling. Key uncertainties include revenue trajectory and clinical-stage risk, both unquantified in available data. The wide gap between methods reflects early-stage execution risk and heterogeneity within the frontier biotech peer set.
